chunks: He gathered its clouds after the separation of its flashes and the distinction of its lightning.

So when the depth of the cloud mass gave birth to rain within it, and its lightning flashed on its sides, and its gleam did not sleep in the depth of its arch and accumulated clouds, He sent it down as a continuous rain, its edges having bent low, the south wind rubbing the peaks of its hills, and shaking its sides.

So when the cloud cast its rain on both its sides, and discharged what it had taken upon itself of the burden carried on it, He brought forth from the plains of the earth the vegetation, and from the tops of the mountains the herbs. So it rejoices in the adornment of its gardens, and delights in what was dressed upon it of the ribbons of its flowers, and the ornaments of what it was shed with of its fresh lights.
And He made that a provision for mankind, and sustenance for livestock, and He broke the paths in its horizons, and established the minarets for the travelers on the broad roads of it.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the process of rain formation and its benefits in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Al-Ashbaah*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs rich rhetorical imagery to describe the meteorological processes of cloud formation and rainfall as a divine sign (*ayah*) of God's creative power. The text highlights how rain serves a dual purpose: providing sustenance (*rizq*) for humans and animals, and facilitating travel by softening the earth, thereby illustrating the interconnectedness of natural phenomena and human utility in Shia cosmological thought.
